title: Google Sheets — Add a Row fails with empty required field
problem: The Make Google Sheets > Add a Row module fails because a cell in the spreadsheet is mapped to an empty or null value. Google Sheets may enforce required columns or the cell reference is invalid.
symptoms: Google Sheets Add a Row module fails for some records but succeeds for others
The failing records have an empty or null value in a field mapped to the spreadsheet
Row is not added to the spreadsheet for the failing record

likely_causes.cause: A column mapped to the Google Sheets row contains a null or empty value from the source bundle
The spreadsheet has data validation rules on a column that reject empty or invalid values

diagnosis_steps: Inspect the input bundle of the Google Sheets module for the failing record
Identify which column field has an empty or null value
Check whether the spreadsheet has data validation rules on that column
Add an ifempty() guard or a default value for the failing field

solutions.solution: Use ifempty(1.field; 'default') in the mapping for any field that can be null or empty
solutions.conditions: When empty values are acceptable but need a placeholder in Google Sheets

solutions.solution: Add a filter before the Google Sheets module to skip records where required fields are absent
solutions.conditions: When records with missing data should not be added to the sheet

prevention: Map all Google Sheets columns with ifempty() guards for optional source fields
Check the spreadsheet's data validation rules before building the Make scenario
search_keywords: make google sheets add row empty

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Google Sheets module
origin_details.evidence: Google Sheets Add a Row module is documented in Make Help Center. Empty field handling is consistent with general Make mapping behavior.

evidence.claim: Make's Google Sheets > Add a Row module maps source bundle fields to spreadsheet columns

sequence: some records have empty optional fields
Google Sheets module fails or adds row with invalid data
conditions: Optional source field absent for some records
No ifempty() guard on the column mapping

diagnostic_signals: Google Sheets Add Row fails for some records but not others
Failing records have empty mapped fields in the bundle inspector
Works after adding ifempty() to the mapping
audit_notes: Google Sheets module documented in Make. Empty field behavior is consistent with Make's general mapping model. Data validation rule enforcement is Google Sheets-side and not specifically documented in Make.

title: Google Sheets — Search Rows returns 0 results for existing data
problem: The Make Google Sheets > Search Rows module returns 0 results even though matching rows exist in the spreadsheet. This causes downstream modules to receive no data.
symptoms: Search Rows returns 0 bundles despite matching rows being present in the spreadsheet
The scenario completes with no output
Search works when tested manually with the same criteria

likely_causes.cause: The column used for the search filter does not match the header row label exactly — Make's Search Rows is case-sensitive and space-sensitive for column matching
The search value contains leading/trailing spaces or different casing than the spreadsheet data
The spreadsheet range is not set correctly — rows outside the defined range are not searched

diagnosis_steps: Open the Google Sheets module and check the column filter — verify the column header label matches exactly (including spaces and casing)
Inspect the search value — check for leading/trailing spaces using the trim() function
Verify the sheet name and range are correctly configured to include all rows
Test the search manually in Google Sheets to confirm the rows are findable

solutions.solution: Use trim() on the search value to remove leading/trailing spaces: {{trim(1.search_value)}}
solutions.conditions: When spaces in the search value prevent matching

solutions.solution: Use lower() on both the search value and ensure the spreadsheet data is consistent in casing, or use a case-insensitive search approach
Verify the range configuration in the Search Rows module — ensure it includes all rows in the spreadsheet
solutions.conditions: When the range is too narrow and excludes rows that should be searched

prevention: Use trim() on search values that come from user input or external systems
Verify the column header labels match exactly before building the scenario
search_keywords: make google sheets not finding rows
make google sheets search not working
make google sheets search empty result

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Google Sheets module
origin_details.evidence: Google Sheets Search Rows module documentation describes column filter matching. Case and space sensitivity is consistent with Google Sheets API behavior.

evidence.claim: Make's Google Sheets > Search Rows module filters rows based on column values — the column header must match exactly

conditions: Search value has spaces or wrong casing

diagnostic_signals: Search Rows returns 0 bundles despite matching data existing in the spreadsheet
Running the scenario manually with Run once also returns 0
Search value may contain spaces or have different casing than spreadsheet data
audit_notes: Search Rows module documented in Make. Case/space sensitivity is consistent with Google Sheets API behavior and widely reported in Make Community. Specific Make documentation on this exact behavior was not found verbatim.

title: Google Sheets — Update a Row fails because row number not found
problem: The Make Google Sheets > Update a Row module requires a specific row number to update. If the row number is incorrect, hardcoded, or the row was deleted, the update fails or updates the wrong row.
symptoms: Update a Row module fails or updates the wrong row
A hardcoded row number is used instead of a dynamically found row number
The row number was found in a previous step but the row was deleted before the update ran

likely_causes.cause: A hardcoded row number is used — it refers to a row that no longer exists or is not the intended target
The row number from Search Rows is not correctly mapped to the Update Row module
Rows were inserted or deleted in the spreadsheet between the search and the update, shifting row numbers

diagnosis_steps: Check the row number field in the Update a Row module — is it hardcoded or dynamically mapped?
If dynamically mapped, trace where the row number comes from (typically Google Sheets > Search Rows output)
Inspect the actual row number value in the execution bundle

solutions.solution: Use Google Sheets > Search Rows to find the row, then map the row number from the search result to the Update a Row module
solutions.conditions: When using a hardcoded row number — replace with dynamic row number from Search Rows

solutions.solution: Add a filter after Search Rows to verify a row was found (results > 0) before attempting the update
solutions.conditions: When Search Rows might return 0 results and Update Row should not run in that case

prevention: Never hardcode row numbers in production scenarios — always use a Search Rows step to find the row dynamically
Add a filter after Search Rows to handle the case where no row is found
search_keywords: make google sheets update row not found
make google sheets update wrong row
make google sheets search then update

origin_details.source_name: Make Help Center — Google Sheets module
origin_details.evidence: Google Sheets Update a Row requires a row number. The Search Rows + Update Row pattern is the standard Make approach for conditional updates.

evidence.claim: Make's Google Sheets > Update a Row module requires a row number to identify which row to update

sequence: get row number from search result
update the row using the row number
conditions: Row number must be dynamically obtained from Search Rows

diagnostic_signals: Update Row module fails or updates wrong row
Row number is hardcoded or not mapped from Search Rows output
Rows were added/deleted in the spreadsheet between the search and update
audit_notes: Update a Row requiring a row number is confirmed in Make documentation. The Search + Update pattern is a documented best practice. Row shifting from insertions/deletions is a Google Sheets API behavior.

title: Google Sheets — API quota exceeded (429 or quota error)
problem: When a Make scenario makes many Google Sheets API calls in a short time — typically through an Iterator — the Google Sheets API quota is exceeded. Google returns a 429 or quota-related error.
symptoms: Google Sheets module fails with a 429 or quota error when processing many rows
Error occurs consistently when the Iterator processes a large number of records
Error does not occur when the same scenario runs on a small number of records

likely_causes.cause: An Iterator is calling a Google Sheets module for each record without a delay, exceeding the Google Sheets API per-minute write quota

diagnosis_steps: Count how many records the Iterator processes per execution
Check Google Sheets API quota limits for your account type in Google Cloud Console
Add a Sleep module inside the Iterator loop and retest

solutions.solution: Add a Tools > Sleep module inside the Iterator loop with a delay calculated from the Google Sheets API quota: if the limit is 300 writes/minute, add a 200ms delay between each write
solutions.conditions: When an Iterator makes per-record calls to Google Sheets at high volume

solutions.solution: Use Google Sheets > Add Multiple Rows or batch update approaches to reduce the number of API calls
solutions.conditions: When the use case supports batching rows into a single API call

prevention: Calculate the theoretical API call rate before deploying an Iterator that calls Google Sheets per record
Prefer batch operations (Add Multiple Rows) over per-record operations in Iterator loops
search_keywords: make google sheets too many requests

origin_details.evidence: Google Sheets API enforces per-minute write quotas documented in Google's API usage limits page.

evidence.claim: Google Sheets API enforces per-minute read/write quotas — exceeding them results in 429 responses

modules: Google Sheets > Add a Row (per record)
sequence: Google Sheets module called per record without delay
conditions: High-volume Iterator calling Google Sheets per record

diagnostic_signals: Google Sheets module fails with 429 or quota error
Error occurs for large datasets but not small ones
Error appears after N records are processed (where N corresponds to quota limit)
audit_notes: Google Sheets API quota limits are documented. Make's Sleep module as a rate-limit mitigation is confirmed. Specific quota values may change — not included to avoid stale data.
